# RuntimeActor Boundary

<!-- Generated by go run ./tools/providerruntimeboundarydocs -write-doc. Do not edit by hand. -->

[Back to runtime actor boundary](../runtime-actor-boundary.md)

`internal/agentbridge/runtimeactor` is the mailbox actor that owns one RuntimeID's provider execution capacity. One actor goroutine owns the in-flight task map and slot state.

## Responsibilities

- Run adapter `Detect` during start and reconcile the raw daemon observation into public C3 `ProviderCapability`.
- Include `PolicyBundleVersion` and detected executable fingerprint in the capability fingerprint input.
- Fail closed for max-concurrent slot exhaustion, duplicate task id, unavailable provider, and unknown provider.
- Submit tasks to `session.Start` and attach an optional `ProtocolDriverProvider` to the session.
- Cascade `Cancel` and `Stop` through session cancellation, process kill, and slot release.
- Project `Status` and `HeartbeatPayload` for local settings UI and control-plane heartbeat consumers.
- An inconclusive authentication/version/probe refresh must preserve the last observed executable/capability identity for running sessions when the executable path and content hash match and no different version was observed. It reports unknown health, denies new submissions and retries after the existing TTL. A confirmed executable/version change still blocks pinned runs.
- Confirmed login-required with the same executable identity makes the provider unavailable and terminates its running sessions as provider_blocked with a bounded authentication-required reason, not runtime-pin drift. Authentication failure never triggers replay or automatic login. If binary identity also changes, runtime-pin fencing takes precedence. A probe error cannot admit work using stale availability.
- Capability refresh on Submit must fence existing sessions against a confirmed executable/version change just like Status refresh; changing the cached capability cannot erase a running session pin.
- RIID-5822/5823 periodic Detect runs outside the runtime mailbox, with at most one probe per provider. Status returns the last immutable observation immediately; only a Submit requiring fresh capability waits in a bounded provider queue.
- Apply asynchronous probe results only for the current generation and captured capability fingerprint. Cancellation, Stop and unrelated provider work remain responsive; Stop cancels probes and refuses queued submissions. Probe failure does not replay an execution or declare recovery.

## Nonresponsibilities

- Supervisor polling, task claim, and runtime selection.
- EventIngestor append and task transition decisions.
- Workdir preparation and native config injection.
- Provider-specific parser or adapter implementation.
- Task DB, project, MWSD, local API, SaaS transport, or infra persistence.
